summary: Charles Henry Tawney was an Indology scholar who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1856–1860). He served as a fellow and tutor at Cambridge (1860), held posts at Presidency University (1866–1892), and was librarian at the India Office Library (1892–1903).

Charles Li works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of British Columbia (attested 2020) and a post as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris (~1948–1954). He held posts at the University of Lyon (~1965–1972) and served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1979–1999).
Charles Oman was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at New College (~1878–1883). He held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1883 to 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1883–1887), later holding a post at SOAS University of London from around 1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the East India Company College and Haileybury, and under traditional teachers in India (~1820–1825). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and as Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who studied at Durham University and under Michael Aris (~1982–1985). He held posts at Tribhuvan University, Oxford (2002–2005), and École Pratique des Hautes Études as professor and Directeur d'études starting in 2009.

Charles Rieu was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Geneva and the University of Bonn, learning under Lassen, Humbert, Freytag, and Gildemeister. He served at the British Museum and the University of Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale under Whitney, Hadley, Woolsey, and Dana, and in Germany under Roth, Weber, Curtius, and Leskien. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1880) and Harvard University (1880–1926).

Charles S. Prebish is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007).

Charles Taliaferro is a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Harvard Divinity School, and Brown University. He served as a professor at St. Olaf College from approximately 1985 to 2022.

Charles Taylor is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1949–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961). He held professorial posts at McGill University (~1961–1998), the University of Montreal (~1967–1973), and Northwestern University (~2002).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and held a post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist who studied under Kalinatha (~1778–1785). A founding member of The Asiatic Society (1784), he served as Oriental Librarian for the East India Company and as Librarian of the India Office Library.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin was a Sinology, Iranian, and Indology scholar who earned a doctorate in law at the University of Liège (~1850–1855). He directed Collège Saint-Quirin and served as professor of Oriental languages at KU Leuven / UCL (~1871–1899).

Charlotte Furth was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. She held academic posts as a professor at California State University (~1966–1989) and subsequently at the University of Southern California (~1989–2008).

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, and Dorje Dradul. He succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities. She served in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000) and founded Sakyadhita and the journal Yasodhara.

Chen-kuo Lin is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Temple University (Ph.D. 1991). He held professorships at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–2018), the European Chair of Chinese Studies at Leiden, and a visiting post at IIAS.
Cheng Yen is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
